title: The full pipeline, auto-ingesting and rewriting a real document through brain.reason
goal: Prove, end to end and through the single lab.common.brain.reason entry point (not a hand-assembled call sequence), that a real, previously-unseen document can be given as raw text plus an ask and come out the other side as a cited, consistency-checked, formatted .docx -- with dslim/bert-base-NER (EXP-080) actually live in the loop, not just standalone-measured -- and report honestly what a real document's density does to the generative rewriter's fidelity gate along the way.
method: A real ~2,400-word, 13-article GDPR excerpt (fetched live from gdpr-info.eu, embedded here as a fixture for reproducibility) auto-chunked by lab.common.ingest.chunk_document into 69 passages, then passed with an ask to lab.common.brain.reason(use_real_ner=True) -- the real dispatch path -- and, to capture the .docx/.md file outputs brain.reason's own signature doesn't expose, an identical lab.common.longform.write_long_document call with the same inputs plus out_path/docx_out_path.

ask_tried_first.text: Rewrite this regulation into a clear, well-organized compliance summary.

ask_that_fires.text: Write a document summarizing this regulation in plain language.

results_prose: Auto-chunked a real 2,368-word, 13-article GDPR excerpt into 69 passages with no manual pre-structuring. 'Rewrite this regulation into a clear, well-organized compliance summary.' (the phrasing tried by hand first) scores 0.6795 against wants_document's 0.75 threshold -- does NOT fire. 'Write a document summarizing this regulation in plain language.' scores 0.7846 -- fires. Calling lab.common.brain.reason with the firing ask and the raw passages (use_real_ner=True) dispatched to lab.common.longform as expected and returned decision='supported_with_flags' with 69 citations. Of 19 leaves written, 0 used flan-t5-small's generation and 19 fell back to the deterministic extractive path -- all of them, driven mainly by ['citations', 'nli'] gate failures (dense modal/numeric regulatory language). 11 cross-page consistency flag(s) were raised, mostly the generic subjects 'the controller'/'the data subject' recurring across unrelated articles with different objects -- a known heuristic limitation of same-subject+same-verb matching on a document this repetitive, not necessarily genuine contradictions. Both a .docx (19 sections, 69 citations) and a .md (2684 words) were written to disk.
conclusion: The full pipeline -- raw text to chunks to entity-grouped outline to fidelity-gated rewrite to cross-page consistency check to a real .docx -- runs end to end on a genuine, previously-unseen document through the single brain.reason entry point, with dslim/bert-base-NER live in the loop (not just separately measured, EXP-080). But the honest, load-bearing result is the fidelity gate's behavior on real text: GDPR's dense modal/numeric legal language defeated flan-t5-small's generation on every leaf, so this run is a working, well-structured extractive assembler on this document, not yet a demonstrated generative rewriter at this density -- exactly the gap EXP-048/077 already flagged for toy and synthetic leaves, now confirmed on real text too, not assumed fixed by wiring alone. Separately, wants_document's threshold is measurably phrasing-sensitive: a natural 'rewrite X' ask the pipeline's own builder tried first does not cross it, while 'write a document summarizing X' does -- a usability gap for a user who does not already know this signal's calibration.
scale_down: One real document (69 passages, 19 leaves) -- a genuine end-to-end proof, not a benchmark across many documents or domains.
follow_ups: flan-t5-small's fidelity gate rejected generation on 100% of this document's leaves -- a larger or fine-tuned checkpoint (e.g. the registered nagbhaskar55/gemma-3-270m-bhaskar-finetune, EXP-076) should be re-run on this identical fixture to see whether a better generator changes this result, or whether dense regulatory language defeats the gate regardless of checkpoint.

wants_document's threshold (tau=0.75) is phrasing-sensitive enough that a natural first attempt ('rewrite this regulation...') fails to fire it -- worth either lowering tau with a wider calibration set (EXP-079 only calibrated against 3 document asks and 4 lookup asks) or accepting the current precision/recall tradeoff explicitly rather than by accident.

The cross-page consistency checker's false-positive rate on repetitive legal text (same generic subject, many unrelated clauses) was not measured here, only observed qualitatively -- a dedicated precision measurement (how many of the 11 flags are genuine contradictions vs. same-subject coincidences) is a real follow-up before trusting this flag on this kind of document.
models_used: dslim/bert-base-NER (entity detection, live via use_real_ner=True, not generative) + flan-t5-small (bounded rewriter role, fidelity-gated, fell back to deterministic extraction on every leaf this run) via lab.common.rewriter_backends.
